s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's phone-cleaning rule appears in the 3.1 partner form, the 3.5 Customers code and the 3.3 reminders. It becomes one sub-workflow.

SUB · Normalise phone

  1. Trigger: When Executed by Another Workflow. Input data mode: define using fields. Fields: id (string), phone (string).
  2. Code node: 
    // SUB · Normalise phone · Code node, Run Once for Each Item
const d = String($json.phone ?? '').replace(/\D/g, '');
const phone = !d ? '' : d.startsWith('234') ? '+' + d : '+234' + d.replace(/^0/, '');
return { json: { id: $json.id, phone, phone_ok: phone.length === 14 } };

The last node's output is what returns to the parent: one item per input, with id, phone and phone_ok.

Parent 1, HL · Partner form → Leads: after the Form Trigger, Edit Fields adds id = {{ $execution.id }}. Execute Sub-workflow (choose SUB · Normalise phone, map id and phone). Because only the defined fields come back, a Merge (combine by matching field id, enrich Input 1) puts the clean phone back onto the full lead before the Sheets node.

Parent 2, HL · Customers nightly: Orders → Execute Sub-workflow (id = order_id, phone = phone) → Merge on id → the 3.5 Code node, with its own normPhone removed.

CheckBeforeAfter
Customers from 12 sample rows6, Chef Tunde first at ₦164,0006, Chef Tunde first at ₦164,000
Five test leads' phonesall +234…identical
Edit the sub: phone_ok also requires a 7, 8 or 9 after +234n/aboth parents show the new phone_ok values in their next run

Write in the log: the sub-workflow's name, its two input fields, and its two callers.
mistakes: Accepting all data instead of defining input fields, so the contract between parent and sub isn't clear.
Forgetting that only the sub's last node output returns, so the parent loses its other fields.
Calling the sub from only one parent, so "change once, both change" is never proven.
Naming it something vague like "My workflow 4" instead of SUB · Normalise phone.
s.pass: A SUB · workflow with defined input fields, called from two parents whose outputs match their earlier results, plus evidence that one edit in the sub changed both parents' next runs.
s.redo: Send it back if either parent's output changed unexpectedly, fields were lost, or only one caller exists.

g.answer:
Worked example: HL · Error alerts after one week of Harvest Lane incidents.

Flow: Error Trigger → Edit Fields · Format (as in the lesson) → Google Sheets append to Incidents → Telegram → Switch. Switch rule 0: {{ $('Format').item.json.message.toLowerCase() }} contains "401" OR contains "credential" → Gmail to Tolu, subject "Reconnect needed: {{ $('Format').item.json.workflow }}". Read from the Format node, because after the Telegram node $json is Telegram's reply, not the error. Fallback → No Operation (Telegram already went).

Incidents sheet (time, workflow, node, message, run URL filled by n8n; cause, fix, minutes filled by Tolu):

TimeWorkflowNodeMessageCauseFixMin
Mon 03:12Supplier pricesSupplier API429 - Too Many RequestsInterval too short after supplier tightened limitInterval 500 → 1,000 ms25
Tue 06:30Morning weatherGoogle Sheets401 credential expiredGoogle sign-in revokedReconnected credential10
Wed 18:00Evening OutboxBuild messageCannot read properties of undefinedCustomer row with blank nameAdded name fallback15
Thu 03:12Supplier pricesSupplier API429 - Too Many RequestsSame as Monday, before fix was publishedPublished the fix5

The 401 row reached Tolu by email as well as Telegram; the others by Telegram only.

Three lessons:

  1. Saving a fix isn't enough: publish it, or the same incident returns (Thursday).
  2. Credential failures need a person, so email beats a chat alert that scrolls away.
  3. Blank customer fields cause most message errors: add fallbacks wherever a name is used.

Changed because of the log: Supplier prices interval raised to 1,000 ms. Submit: the Incidents sheet, one Telegram and one email screenshot, and the before/after of the changed setting.
mistakes: Leaving cause and fix blank on most rows, so the log never teaches anything.
Matching "Credential" case-sensitively, so some credential errors miss the email route.
Logging incidents only from manual test runs, which don't fire the error workflow.
Writing lessons with no workflow change to show for them.
g.pass: An Incidents sheet with a row for every failure in the week, each with cause, fix and minutes; proof that a credential or 401 failure arrived by email; three lessons; and one workflow changed because of the log.
g.redo: Send it back if rows lack causes and fixes, the email route was never shown working, or no workflow was changed.
